# Targeted street indexed-copy proof

This diagnostic compares exact original `75906273c0cd414c0d004320fc6f654b4783e5b1` with candidate `027f6c7627e21a53be32c586764fe2a02aa0e3a3` (tree `8897d4009b8c117f5f241ca2bc81d21b769f63c4`). `pins.json` declares exactly eight permitted candidate changes: the five reviewed street implementation/test files and the three unchanged PR270 hover-harness repair files. Every other original leaf, including the original performance driver, must be identical. The candidate has only the original759 parent.

This is a diagnostic-only targeted street scene, not a full-world, FPS, original ride, controls-deadline or release acceptance. Native Metal and SwiftShader results remain separate. No allocation reduction is a measured speed claim.

## Source and scene binding

The driver reads Git objects, never mutable application worktree files. The original `StaticPaletteBatch` bytes occupy an adjacent virtual module beside the candidate class; their unchanged relative imports have the same module identities. Thus both classes use the same Three r185.1, ordering and atmosphere WeakMaps, materials, source meshes and textures. Exact class/helper copies, original source inventory, transformation receipt and compiled bundle are retained.

The browser constructs the original palette and candidate palette consecutively before adding either root and performing the common `WorldAtmosphere.flush`. It checks that candidate construction does not change the shared material callbacks, keys or versions. This sequence avoids an atmosphere rediscovery between the two original identity guards. Only the candidate constructor receives the already-authoritative factory street set as its fourth argument.

The original street factory, all 59 original asset files and the original atmosphere/realistic/photo/sunset composition are used. The original private `cloudTexture` function is extracted byte-for-byte from pinned `islandSky.ts`, with only a shared Three import and named export wrapper. No world factory, shader expression, texture format, normal, triangle, collision or original geometry is rewritten. The existing fixture's 960×600 viewport, antialiasing, tone mapping, camera lens, ordinary caster, ground, lights and shadow-map resolution remain unchanged. The original atmosphere composition is added because the older small fixture omitted it; its fixed time/cloud/day inputs are recorded and shared across both lanes.

## Fixed cases and positive controls

`plan.json` was frozen from original geometry before any browser result. It contains five poses × day/night × shadow on/off = 20 cases per backend. The three inherited poses are west, conservatory and northeast. The two authored grade poses target the maximum absolute-grade white primitive of length at least one metre in tiles `0,0` and `1,3`, breaking ties by original record ordinal. Each camera is 32 metres behind, five metres sideways and six metres above that original primitive. These are source-authored diagnostic cameras, not captured failing-control cameras.

The grade camera/target pairs are:

- `(82.18434504700853, 10.43800016026944, 122.71524407607887)` → `(76.30000305175781, 4.438000160269439, 90.86599731445312)`.
- `(447.64176554896915, 9.886000114493072, 796.8810126608449)` → `(441.8160095214844, 3.886000114493072, 828.7410278320312)`.

Every one of the seven native groups has a predeclared visibility control. Their source-only planning receipts retain original triangle coordinates and the closest original ray hit at a fixed pixel. Such a ray witness is not a rendered-pixel claim: the actual run must remove that exact display group and change at least one whole-frame pixel. Original and indexed hidden-group frames must still be identical; restoring the original group must exactly recover the original frame. The predeclared west/day shadow control likewise removes only the directional light's shadow membership and restores it. Controls cannot be relocated, masked or relaxed after a result.

Each case captures original A, candidate B and restored A after three fenced warm renders per lane. Complete RGBA8 pixels must have zero differences and zero tolerance. All actual shadow-target color attachments, matrix bytes, original visibility and normalized native draw sequences are checked too. Native depth-texture bytes are not claimed.

## Native geometry, order and programs

All seven groups must reach real `WEBGL_multi_draw` submissions. Original A must use arrays; B must use elements. The curb aggregate must be Uint32 with 1,052,074 unique tuples. The other six groups use Uint16. The proof reads complete actual native position/normal/index buffers through `COPY_READ_BUFFER`, restores that binding, verifies the upload against the constructed arrays, and retains raw bytes.

The independent Node audit expands B's indices and compares every original Float32 position/normal bit in original triangle order, including signed zero and degenerate triangles. It also checks first-encounter tuple order, tile-local index ranges and native aggregate capacities. Native byte offsets are normalized by the actual index width and source geometry range; numerical offsets from drawArrays and drawElements are not compared directly. Original source IDs, instance IDs, original depth/source-ID sort, culling, programs, uniforms and submitted matrices must agree.

Every original street geometry/raycast identity, index, attributes, bounds, draw range, material identity and bytes is recorded before/after. Original ray results retain face/vertex IDs. Display roots retain the production no-op raycast convention.

Full actual attached shader sources, native program identities, reflection, user-attribute bindings, uniform values and texture bindings are retained. Within one backend, corresponding submissions must select the same native programs. No cross-backend program, buffer, texture or reflection-order equality is assumed. Reflection may expose the known built-in `gl_VertexID` with size1/typeINT/location−1; it is retained as a built-in, with no invented user buffer. Unknown built-ins or negative user-attribute locations fail. A street morph-target define is prohibited. The inactive original Three morph source is retained without rewriting.

## Fixed timing and bounds

After correctness and restored controls for each case, two fixed blocks are measured: ABBA, then BAAB. Each query covers exactly one render. That yields 160 queries per backend, four original and four indexed samples per case. Readbacks, gzip, hashing and persistence are outside the queries. Every raw timer, disjoint flag, CPU submission duration and separate completion-fence wait is retained. A missing GPU timer, timeout or disjoint remains a failure/unavailable result; no sample or backend is replaced. One constructor observation per class is separately labeled unbalanced startup information.

The workflow has one macos-15 Metal job and one ubuntu-24.04 SwiftShader job, original attempts only, 40 minutes per job. The browser/driver uses a fixed 35-minute run bound, 30-second fences/query waits and 10-second owned cleanup. Errors, failed requests, late failures during artifact validation and incomplete cleanup all prohibit a passing verdict. Failed jobs still upload available raw evidence. Both original backend results must be reviewed; one passing lane never substitutes for the other.

## Local source-only validation

`node --test contract.test.mjs` checks provenance gates, native offset normalization, strict reflection, independent PNG corruption handling, exact binary counts and late-error finalization. Compilation may use `--compile-only --compile-tree-only` against the verified local immutable tree while the remote commit object is not hydrated. Its report explicitly lacks local commit-to-tree verification and can never launch a browser. Normal execution must independently fetch/verify the immutable candidate commit, tree, sole parent and eight-path recipe first.

No local browser execution or CI run is part of preparation. Real Metal/SwiftShader equality, GPU benefit, startup cost and original acceptance remain unmeasured until the separately authorized first runs complete.
